title: Game 13: Morrison–Capablanca
subtitle: Restrict a bishop, then attack with every piece

steps.title: A strong bishop on the long diagonal

narration.say: Morrison has White against Capablanca at New York in 1918. Black prepares a kingside fianchetto in the Ruy Lopez.
White pins the knight. Black develops the bishop to g7 and castles.
White castles on the opposite wing and places both rooks in the centre.

steps.title: Challenge the bishop before it can attack

narration.say: Black can drive the bishop away and gain kingside space.

exercise.prompt: Black to move. Attack the bishop on h4.

narration.say: Black unblocks the bishop on g7 by moving the knight to h5.

exercise.prompt: Black to move. Prepare to restrict the bishop on g3.

narration.say: Black pushes f4, restricting the bishop on g3. White tries to open lines, but Black keeps the pawn structure intact.
White brings a rook to h1. Black improves the bishop, then exchanges central knights.
The white bishop retreats to h2. Black challenges the remaining knight.
Black takes e4. White exchanges the bishop for the knight and captures f4.
Black activates the queen. The queens are exchanged, but the attack continues.

steps.title: Bring the last available piece into action

narration.say: White retreats the king to a1. Black’s remaining rook can now join the attack.

exercise.prompt: Black to move. Bring the rook from a8 to e8.

narration.say: Black checks on the first rank and exchanges one pair of rooks.
White’s king advances, but Black opens the centre with d5.
Black’s rook gives checks and wins material.

steps.title: Stop before an ambiguous final transcription

narration.say: The supplied TeX next prints d7, although White has just moved a rook to d8. The expected rook notation is missing. This lesson stops after Kh7 rather than playing an unverified final move.
The book records Black’s win. The decisive theme is the coordinated activity of both rooks and the bishops.

steps.title: A restricted piece changes the practical balance

narration.say: Black used pawn advances to restrict White’s bishop, while retaining control of the centre.
The attack survived the queen exchange because Black’s other pieces were active.
The arrival of the last rook turned the positional advantage into a direct attack.
